STRUCTURE read off the paper's own printed General Instructions on idx 2 and it matches `term2_sci` EXACTLY and agrees with the dispatch: 12 questions, all compulsory, THREE sections; Section A Q1-3 @2, Section B Q4-11 @3, Section C Q12 a case-study based question @5. 6 + 24 + 5 = 35, and the marking scheme's own instruction 10 independently says 'A full scale of marks 35 has to be used'. ****THE DISPATCH WAS RIGHT AND `wave.ts` IS WRONG: THIS PAPER DOES CONTAIN MCQs.**** Section C's case study Q12 is FIVE one-mark MCQs, (i) to (v), each with four printed options, and the marking scheme keys all five in its own SECTION-C table, in the `(i)-a` em-dash convention: '12. Degree signs are printed as a superscript 'o' throughout and are transcribed as `^\circ`. OUT-OF-SYLLABUS: none. Every topic here (rectifier, photodiode, alpha-scattering, lenses, single-slit diffraction, hydrogen spectral series, compound microscope, photoelectric effect, fission Q-value, EM spectrum, reflecting telescope, prism, diode V-I, total internal reflection) has a live chapter, so no `[Outdated]` chapter was needed and none was invented. plan.txt names no reference paper ('No reference papers given - transcribe every question'), and per the follower instruction EVERY question was transcribed regardless. Every other 'Draw V-I characteristics / With the help of a ray diagram' instruction on this paper is the STUDENT drawing and is deliberately NOT flagged. ****ONE-WORD DIVERGENCE FROM THE OPENER IN THE SHARED CASE-STUDY PASSAGE:**** this paper prints 'If the angle of incidence is increased FURTHER the ray will not emerge', confirmed at 6x magnification on idx 12; the committed 55/5/1 file reads 'farther'. questions._figure: REQUIRED - the stem says only 'as shown in the figure' and names no angle at all, so the prism's geometry, the internal ray's orientation AND the ray's fate at face AC all exist only in the drawing. Page idx 10. READ ON THIS PAPER'S OWN PAGE at 2x and again at 4x on the region around N, not copied from 55/5/1. DESCRIBED (labelling and layout only): a triangular prism drawn with apex A at the top, B at the bottom left and C at the bottom right, the base BC horizontal; an angle value is printed inside the triangle at A and another at B; the refractive index is printed inside the triangle as the symbol mu set equal to a surd; a ray arrives from the lower left carrying an arrowhead and meets face AB at a point labelled M; a dotted normal is drawn at M and the angle between the ray and that normal, inside the glass, is labelled r1 against an arc; the ray inside the prism runs from M to a point labelled N on face AC and carries an arrowhead; a dotted normal is drawn at N and the angle there is labelled r2 against an arc; a ray leaves N carrying two further arrowheads. WITHHELD deliberately, because each is exactly what the question tests: the two printed angle VALUES at A and B; the ORIENTATION of the internal ray MN relative to the base BC, which is what fixes r2 and hence both sub-answers; and the direction the ray takes at face AC relative to that face, which is what sub-part (i) turns on - the marking scheme's own answer opens 'As the emergent ray grazes along the side AC'. questions.context: A ray of light travels from a denser to a rarer medium. After refraction, it bends away from the normal. When we keep increasing the angle of incidence, the angle of refraction also increases till the refracted ray grazes along the interface of two media. The angle of incidence for which it happens is called critical angle. If the angle of incidence is increased further the ray will not emerge and it will be reflected back in the denser medium. This phenomenon is called total internal reflection of light.
questions.stem: A ray of light travels from a medium into water at an angle of incidence of \(18^\circ\).
